Unofficial until approved by the

  MINUTES
  Adjourned Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  April 28, 2025
  5:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 5:10 p.m., on Monday, April 28, 2025, the Alhambra City Council met in the Council
Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  MAZA, MALONEY, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Hembree, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director
of Finance Lieu, Director of Community Development Ho, Director of Public Works and Utilities Ahlen,
Chief of Police Kennedy, Chief of Fire Department Ragusa, Director of Library Services LohGuan,
Director of Human Resources Ko, Manager Analyst Alvarez, Public Information Specialist Rodriguez,
Battalion Chief Lawrence, Assistant Chief of Police Fuentes

FLAG SALUTE:  Mayor Lee

LEE: Mayor Lee read the City’s Mission Statement as follows: The City of Alhambra is dedicated to
responsive, creative leadership and quality services, ensuring desirable neighborhoods and a
supportive business environment, while being sensitive to the diversity of our community.

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

PUBLIC COMMENT FOR NON-AGENDIZED ITEMS – F2M25-4

Shuang CHEN expressed her concerns regarding electro-magnetic radiation (EMR) attacks that she
experienced on multiple occasions. She discussed the criminals who attacked her, her mother, and
the toll the attacks have taken.

PRESENTATIONS

1.  STATE OF THE CITY ADDRESS – F2M25-16

  Mayor Lee provided insight on the current state of the City and the progress that were made
  over the past year. Ms. LEE presented the State of the City Address. A copy of the presentation
  is on file in the City Clerk’s office.

MALONEY:  Vice Mayor Maloney left Council Chambers at 5:17 p.m. and returned at 5:20 p.m.

  Discussion:  None.

4-28-25
   Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the informational report.

2.  HAZARD MITIGATION PLAN UPDATE – F2M23-70

  Battalion Chief LAWRENCE delivered a staff report. Rob FLANER, from Black & Veatch,
  delivered a presentation, which is on file in the City Clerk’s office. The Local Hazard Mitigation
  Plan (LHMP) is a federally required document that guides our community in making decisions
  and developing policies to reduce or eliminate risks to life and property. The plan identifies the
  types of hazards that threaten our community, evaluates our vulnerability to those threats, and
  outlines a strategy to reduce or eliminate the risk posed by those threats. The Federal Disaster
  Mitigation Act of 2000 requires that a community have an approved hazard mitigation plan to
  be eligible to apply for and receive certain types of FEMA hazard mitigation funds. The City of
  Alhambra has been in the process of developing its first Local Hazard Mitigation Plan. This
  presentation aimed to inform the City Council on the Local Hazard Mitigation Plan development
  process, including key phases, public engagement efforts, and next steps.

  Public Comment:  Albert VIERA, 1218 S. Marguerita Ave., requested a project to connect
  local gardeners, especially residents who do not have a yard or area to garden, with
  homeowners who would like to learn about gardening.

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER and Mr. FLANER discussed the
  upcoming community meetings and the issues specific to each Council district. Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER suggested sending the survey to the school district in order to gain more
  responses particularly from residents who speak other languages. She also requested more
  information regarding risk assessment from CalFire.

  Vice Mayor MALONEY discussed the hazards presented and further discussed risks
  presented by fire, earthquake, and extreme heat. He also expressed hope that the
  Sustainability Plan would help mitigate some of the hazards as a result of climate change. Mr.
  MALONEY and Mr. FLANER discussed the detailed maps which would be presented at the
  upcoming community meetings.

  Councilmember MAZA and WANG thanked Mr. Flaner for the report. Ms. WANG and Mr.
  FLANER discussed the process to develop the plan as well as the strategies to address them.
  Mr. FLANER discussed the ways in which the plan was developed to be a dynamic document
  which could be changed as other policies or programs may affect it in the future and also
  discussed the presentation of the strategic actions of the plan at the community meetings. Ms.
  WANG and Mr. FLANER discussed opportunities for regional collaboration to address hazards
  which may impact City boundaries and discussed the potential for multi-jurisdictional planning.
  Ms. WANG and Mr. FLANER next discussed procuring funding sources for the priorities
  established by the plan. Ms. WANG and Mr. FLANER also discussed ways in which the plan
  would address equity priority groups and identifying socially vulnerable groups in the
  community. Ms. WANG supported Ms. Andrade-Stadler’s suggestion to reach out to the school
  district for more responses.

  Mayor LEE and Mr. FLANER also discussed grant opportunities to procure emergency
  supplies for residents. Ms. LEE went on to discuss public shelter sites identified in the
  Emergency Operational Plan with Battalion Chief LAWRENCE. They also discussed the
  provisions of the Emergency Operational Plan to procure and distribute emergency supplies.
  Battalion Chief LAWRENCE stated that the Emergency Operational Plan was also due for an
  update after the development of the Hazard Mitigation Plan.

4-28-25
   Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the informational report.

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 3 – 21)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda, with the exception of Item No. 11 and 12, were considered
by the City Council to be routine and were enacted by one motion.

3.  CONTRACT AMENDMENT: CUSTODIAL SERVICES FOR ALHAMBRA CITY HALL,
  ALHAMBRA POLICE DEPARTMENT, ALHAMBRA CIVIC CENTER LIBRARY, FIRE
STATION 71 & VARIOUS CITY FACILITIES – F2M22-45, C2M22-41, M2M25-54

  On June 27, 2022, the City Council awarded a custodial services contract for various City
  facilities to Commercial Building Management Services. The contract amount was for
  $2,263,583.47, commencing August 1, 2022 through June 30, 2027. The contract was
  amended twice since award – first to change services and second to reflect a chance in
  company name and ownership. Amendment No. 3 is to correct Sections 4 (Fee) and 8 (Time).
  Although the compensation for FY 2025-26 and 2026-27 were already included in the total
  award, the breakdown of costs was not added in the agreement. Section 4, therefore, was
  amended to state that compensation to contractor shall be in an amount not to exceed
  $464,972.93 for FY 2025-26 and $481,246.96 for FY 2026-27. Section 8 was amended to
  state that the term of the agreement was for a period of five years with an option to extend the
  contract for two one-year terms, as was originally approved. Currently, there was no need to
  execute a contract extension. All other provisions remained unchanged.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a contract amendment to Contract No. C2M22-
  41, subject to final language approval by the City Manager and the City Attorney, to clarify
  language in the existing agreement for custodial services; authorized the City Manager or
  designee to execute the amendment; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to
  finalize the Council’s action. (M2M25-54)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

4.  RENEWAL OF MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH THE ALHAMBRA UNIFIED
  SCHOOL DISTRICT (AUSD) FOR SCHOOL RESOURCE OFFICERS FOR FY 2025-26 –
  F2M20-57, C2M20-37, M2M25-55

  Both the Alhambra Police Department and AUSD believed that the continuation of the School
  Resource Officer (SRO) Program would further the goal of maintaining a safe school
  environment for students and staff. The existing Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with
  AUSD for an SRO Program would expire on June 30, 2025. Renewing this MOU would provide
  police officers to the District during the academic school year calendar through June 30, 2026.
  AUSD would reimburse the City for services in an amount not to exceed $488,340.00 annually.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved that certain Renewal of Memorandum of
  Understanding 2025-2026 with the Alhambra Unified School District on file in the City Clerk’s
  3
4-28-25
   Office as Contract No. C2M20-37 to continue the School Resource Officer Program for Fiscal
  Year 2025-26, contingent upon entry into a reimbursement agreement for the cost of such
  services with AUSD; authorized the Chief of Police to execute the Renewal of the
  Memorandum of Understanding; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to
  finalize Council’s action. (M2M25-55)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

5.  SECOND CONTRACT AMENDMENT WITH ALL CITY MANAGEMENT SERVICES (ACMS)
  FOR SCHOOL CROSSING GUARD SERVICES AND REIMBURSEMENT AGREEMENT
  WITH ALHAMBRA UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT FOR SUMMER SCHOOL CROSSING
  GUARD SERVICES – F2M22-62, C2M23-90, M2M25-56

  On November 13, 2023, City Council awarded a contract to All City Management Services
  (ACMS) for the School Crossing Guard Program for an 18-month period through June 2025 in
  the amount not to exceed $630,262.08. On May 13, 2024, the City Council approved the First
  Amendment to the agreement with ACMS for an additional $68,652.80 and entered into a
  Reimbursement Agreement with the Alhambra Unified School District (AUSD) for summer
  school crossing guard services. Staff requested to amend the contract with ACMS to extend
  the contract to July 31, 2026 and thereby increase the contract by $451,990.56 for a grand
  contract total of $1,150,905.44 to continue the school crossing guard program. An estimated
  $26,772.96 of the amended costs would be subject to AUDS reimbursement.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a second amendment to the contract with All
  City Management Services (C2M23-90) for a total amendment amount not to exceed
  $451,990.56 and a grand contract total of $1,150,905.44, subject to final language approval
  by the City Manager and City Attorney; extended the contract to July 31, 2026, contingent on
  a Reimbursement Agreement with the Alhambra Unified School District for the cost of summer
  school crossing guard services; authorized the City Manager or designee to execute such
  documents; and, authorized staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.
  (M2M25-56)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

6.  RESOLUTION APPROVING A REVISED COMPREHENSIVE MEMORANDUM OF
  UNDERSTANDING (MOU) WITH THE ALHAMBRA POLICE OFFICERS’
  ASSOCIATION (APOA) – F2M25-2, R2M25-19, C87-16C, M2M25-57

  At the April 14, 2025 Council meeting, the City Council received community input regarding
  traffic related concerns. In response and moving forward, the Traffic Division within the Police
  Department would include the addition of Traffic Investigator category. Currently, the Traffic
  Division is comprised of motorcycle officers, thus this new category would allow for an officer
  in a patrol vehicle. The Traffic Investigator’s duties would include patrolling, investigating
  accidents, hit and run and driving under the influence accidents, and traffic related crimes.
  4
4-28-25
   City staff and APOA representatives reached agreement on Special Assignment language for
  this Traffic Investigator position and it was reflected in the proposed revised MOU. There was
  no financial impact as the existing budget was appropriately funded to allow for this position
  within the Traffic Division of the Police Department.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M25-19 entitled: A Resolution
  of the Alhambra City Council approving a Revised Comprehensive Memorandum of
  Understanding between the City of Alhambra and the Alhambra Police Officers’ Association
  that includes a provision for a Special Assignment – Traffic Investigator category; and, directed
  staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M25-57)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

7.  AWARD CONTRACT: 2025 USDA SUMMER FOOD SERVICE PROGRAM – F2M25-25,
  N2M25-18, C2M25-15, M2M25-58

  On February 24, 2025, the City Council approved the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids for
  the 2025 Summer Food Service Program. Staff included the following food vendors in the
  bidding process: Food Service Outreach, Inc., San Gabriel Unified School District, JA Food
  Service, Leo’s Meals, Preferred Meals, Good Heart Catering, School Nutrition Plus, Inc., Unity
  Meals, Bamboo Island Catering, and Everytable. On April 17, 2025, the City Clerk received
  one bid for the program in the amount of $95,942.00. The bid received by School Nutrition
  Plus, Inc. was the lowest responsive bid.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract to School Nutrition Plus, subject to
  the final language approved by the City Manager and City Attorney, in the amount of
  $95,942.00 for the 2025 Summer Food Service Program; and, directed staff to take the steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M25-58)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

8.  CONTRACT AMENDMENT: PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING DESIGN SERVICES
FOR THE BURKE HERITAGE PARK AND MARENGO YARD STORMWATER  CAPTURE
PROJECT – F2M21-63, C2M24-36, M2M25-59

  On May 13, 2024, the City Council awarded a contract for Engineering Design Services for
  the Burke Heritage Park and Marengo Yard Stormwater Capture Project in the amount of
  $784,299. As the design elements progressed, a project site meeting was called to examine
  current site conditions. During the meeting, the City identified necessary improvements at the
  Marengo Yard, which included: stormwater pollution prevention elements such as repaving
  the yard entry area; enhancements to the existing construction material staging area, as well
  as upgrading the property line (security) fence with a steel tubing fence; installing a remote
  5
4-28-25
   access gate; and upgrading the perimeter lighting. Discussions also included upgrading the
  existing onsite restroom facilities. This amendment covered the increased costs to prepare
  plans and specifications (architectural, topographic surveying), additional project
  management, and construction support for the proposed Marengo Yard improvements.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council approved an amendment to the contract C2M24-36 with
  CWE for Engineering Design Services for the Burke Heritage Park and Marengo Yard
  Stormwater Capture Project, subject to final language approval by the City Manager and City
  Attorney, to increase the contract amount by $127,872.00; and, directed staff to undertake the
  steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M25-59)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

9.  AWARD CONTRACT: ALHAMBRA LIT CROSSWALK TRAFFIC CONTROL
  DEVICES PROJECT – F2M22-56, N2M24-151, C2M25-16, M2M25-60

  On December 9, 2024, the City Council authorized the distribution of a Notice of Inviting Bids
  for the Alhambra Lit Crosswalk Traffic Control Devices Project. On February 27, 2025, the
  City Clerk received and opened three bids for the Project ranging from $1,990,425.85
  (California Professional Engineering, Inc.) and $2,494,717.15 (CT&T Concrete Paving Inc.).
  Staff reviewed the bids and found the bid received from California Professional Engineering,
  Inc. in the amount of $1,990,425.85 to be the lowest responsible bid. California Professional
  Engineering, Inc. had the necessary licenses to complete the work and has conducted similar
  scale projects in surrounding cities.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken: City Council awarded contract, subject to final language approval by the City
  Manager and City Attorney, to California Professional Engineering, Inc. in the amount of
  $1,990,425.85 for the Active Transportation Project (ATP) Lit Crosswalk Traffic Control Device
  Project; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.
  (M2M25-60)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

10.  CONTRACT AMENDMENT: LIFE ASSIST INC. FOR THE PURCHASE OF DISPOSABLE
  MEDICAL SUPPLIES – F2M20-6B, C2M20-20, M2M25-61

  On June 8, 2020, the City Council awarded a contract to Life Assist for the purchase of
  disposable medical supplies in the amount not to exceed $90,000 annually. The contract was
  due to expire on June 30, 2025. Life Assist agreed to continue their service for an additional
  two-year term. Due to an unforeseen rise in essential purchases and with the rising costs of
  medical supplies, the entire contract was spent for FY 2024-25. A contingency in the amount
  of $35,000 was required to continue to the necessary purchases for the remainder of this fiscal
  6
4-28-25
   year. The Fire Department would like to continue to work with Life Assist. Pursuant to
  Alhambra Municipal Code Chapter 3.36.080 (E), the City Council may, by majority vote, waive
  the purchasing procedures to fit a specific purchase. In this case, the contract extension
  provided maintaining high-quality service, product inventory and availability despite industry
  shortages. Therefore, staff recommended the City Council award the two-year contract
  extension and waive the bid process.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved an amendment to the contract between the City
  of Alhambra and Life Assist Inc. (C2M20-20) for an additional amount of $35,000 to reflect a
  not to exceed amount of $125,000 per year and extend the contract for an additional two-year
  term, subject to final language approval by the City Manager and City Attorney; authorized
  additional appropriations to satisfy upcoming fiscal year budget expenditures related to this
  contract; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.
  (M2M25-61)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

11.  AWARD CONTRACT: 2024 CDBG ADA RAMP PROJECT – F2M25-26, N2M25-20,
C2M25-17, M2M25-62

  On February 24, 2025, the City Council authorized circulating a Notice of Inviting Bids for the
  2024 CDBG ADA Ramp Project. On March 27, 2025, the City Clerk received 5 bids ranging
  from base bid amounts of $430,575.00 (TVR Construction Engineering) to $503,000.00
  (Carter Enterprises Group DBA Pavement Rehab Co.). TVR Construction Engineering (TVR)
  submitted the lowest bid. However, during the bid evaluation process it was discovered that
  TVR failed to submit a completed subcontractor list as required by the Notice of Inviting Bids.
  Therefore, the bid from TVR was deemed non-responsive. The second lowest bidder, CJ
  Concrete Construction, Inc., was deemed the lowest bidder. According to Public Contract
  Code, the award is based on the lowest base bid. In addition to the Base Bid amount, CJ
  Concrete Construction, Inc. submitted $158,400.00 under the Alternative Bid Schedule for 8
  additional locations and asphalt repair. Staff reviewed the bids and found the bid received from
  CJ Concrete Construction, Inc. in the amount of $638,125.00 to be the lowest responsible bid.
  CJ Concrete Construction, Inc. had the necessary licenses to complete the work and has
  conducted similar scale projects in surrounding cities.

  Public Comment:  Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., discussed the funding for the
  project and expressed concern using CDBG funds for projects other than housing. Mr.
  McCAMMON also discussed the history of the Americans with Disabilities Act.

  Discussion:  None.
  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to CJ Concrete Construction, Inc. in the amount of
  $638,125.00 for the 2024 CDBG ADA Ramp Project; and, directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M25-62)
  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

4-28-25
 12.  AWARD CONTRACT: FY 2023-2024 SB1 STREET REHABILITATION PROJECT –
F2M23-38, N2M24-153, C2M25-18, M2M25-63

  The FY 23-24 SB1 Street Rehabilitation Project was located in the northeast area of the City.
  The project consisted of residential streets within the Lindaraxa Park Historic Neighborhood
  and Bean Tract Historic Neighborhood. The City Council approved the circulation of a Notice
  Inviting Bids on December 9, 2024. On February 27, 2025, the City Clerk received 6 bids
  ranging from $3,085,000.00 (Hardy & Harper) to $4,049,153.00 (Toro). Staff reviewed the bids
  and found the bid received from Hardy & Harper, Inc. in the amount of $3,085,000.00 was the
  lowest responsible bid. Hardy & Harper, Inc. had the necessary licenses to complete the work
  and has conducted similar scale projects in surrounding cities.

  Public Comment:
  1) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova Ave., discussed the project at 801 E. Main and the
  ways it could potentially affect the SB1 project. He also requested staff review addressing
  issues on nearby streets.

  2) Bertha RIVERA discussed additional streets which needed improvements, discussed the
  need to notify surrounding neighbors of street improvement projects, and discussed the
  impact of large construction trucks in residential areas.

  Discussion: Mayor LEE and City Manager BINNQUIST discussed the notification process
  for street improvement projects. Ms. LEE requested additional information. Councilmember
  WANG supported Ms. Lee’s suggestion, and further requested that the project manager
  include notification programs in the contract.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to Hardy & Harper, Inc. in the amount of $3,085,000.00
  for the FY 23-24 SB1 Street Rehabilitation Project; and, directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M25-63)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

13.  AWARD CONTRACT: ALLEY REHABILITATION PROJECT (AREA A - PHASE II) –
  F2M25-27, N2M25-21, C2M25-19, M2M25-64

  On February 24, 2025, the City Council authorized circulating a Notice of Inviting Bids the for
  the Alley Rehabilitation Project (Area A / Phase II). On April 3, 2025, the City Clerk received
  4 bids ranging from base bid amounts of $738,535.00 (Kalban, Inc.) to $1,087,287.60 (DASH
  Construction Company). According to Public Contract Code, the award is based on the lowest
  base bid. In addition to the Base Bid amount, Kalban, Inc. submitted $238,250.00 under the
  Alternative Bid Schedule A for the East/West alley south of Ramona Road between
  Westminster Avenue and Garvey Avenue. Staff reviewed the bids and found the bid received
  from Kalban, Inc. in the amount of $976,785.00 to be the lowest responsible bid. Kalban, Inc.
  had the necessary licenses to complete the work and has conducted similar scale projects in
  surrounding cities.

  Discussion:  None.

  8
4-28-25
   Action Taken:  City Council awarded contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to Kalban, Inc. in the amount of $976,785.00 for the Alley
  Rehabilitation Project (Area A/Phase II); and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary
  to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M25-64)

  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

14.  AWARD CONTRACT: PURCHASE OF ONE UTILITY TRUCK FOR THE PUBLIC
  WORKS DEPARTMENT – F2M25-6A, C2M25-20, M2M25-65

  The 2024-25 Fiscal Year Budget included funding for replacing one Utility vehicle. Staff located
  and solicited quotes for one Ford F-250 utility truck. This was to replace an older, less fuel-
  efficient, high-mileage vehicle. Pursuant to the City Council’s authority under Alhambra
  Municipal Code Section 3.36.080(E), the City Council may dispense with further procedures
  and enter into a contract when it meets a specific purchase need. In this instance, staff
  intended to secure the utility truck under cooperative purchase through Sourcewell at a cost
  of $78,449.71. Ford of Long Beach, however, has a vehicle in stock and quoted the City the
  price of $67,635.57. Staff recommended issuing Ford of Long Beach a contract to purchase
  the new Ford F-250 utility truck.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to Ford of Long Beach for the purchase of one new Ford
  F-250 Utility Truck in an amount not to exceed $67,635.57; and, directed staff to undertake
  the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M25-65)

19.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF AN ORDINANCE AMENDING CHAPTERS 3.36,
  3.38, AND 3.40 CONCERNING BIDDING AND CONTRACTING THRESHOLDS DUE TO
  AMENDMENTS TO CUPCCAA, AND SECTION 9.74.060 CONCERNING FALSE ALARMS
  – F2M25-16, O2M25-4845

  Staff requested that the City Council declare introduced for second reading and adopt an
  Ordinance amending Chapters 3.36, 3.38, and 3.40 concerning bidding and contracting
  thresholds due to amendments to CUPCCAA, and Section 9.74.060 concerning false alarms.
  Periodically amendments are needed to the Alhambra Municipal Code (“AMC”) based upon
  changes in legislation and issues arising in implementation of the AMC. This ordinance made
  amendments to the AMC in two areas. Last Fall the City Council adopted Ordinance No.
  10
4-28-25
   O2M24-4837 which implemented the California Uniform Public Construction Cost Accounting
  Act (“CUPCCAA”), allowing for more expedited contracting for public works projects. That
  same ordinance also adjusted the various bidding thresholds throughout the AMC for other
  types of contracts to make the thresholds uniform across contracts. AB 2192, which went into
  effect January 1, 2025, increased some of the CUPCCAA thresholds: the $60,000 threshold
  was raised to $75,000 and the $200,000 threshold was raised to $220,000. An adjustment to
  these thresholds was necessary to come into compliance with CUPCCAA. Additionally,
  changes to similar thresholds for other contracts was recommended for consistency, in the
  same manner that was recommended when Ordinance No. O2M24-2837 was originally
  adopted. The second recommended area for amendment to the AMC related to false alarm
  fees. Under the AMC, after 3 false home alarms within a year, fees would be charged for
  additional responses. The code provided that the Police Chief, may waive those fees. This
  level of discretion was called out elsewhere in the code, but typically the City Council has
  reserved such discretion to itself. City staff would recommend deleting the provision providing
  such discretion to City staff. The City Council gave first reading to this ordinance at the April
  14, 2025 Council meeting.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council declared introduced for its second reading and adopted
  the following ordinance entitled:

  Ordinance No O2M25-4845: An Ordinance of the Alhambra City Council
  amending Chapters 3.36, 3.38, and 3.40 concerning bidding and contracting
  thresholds due to amendments to CUPCCAA, and Section 9.74.060
  concerning false alarms

  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG, LEE

20.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF AN ORDINANCE APPROVING AN UPDATED
  AB 481 POLICY FOR THE USE OF MILITARY EQUIPMENT BY THE ALHAMBRA POLICE
  DEPARTMENT – F2M22-41, O2M25-4843

  Staff requested that the City Council declare introduced for second reading and adopt an
  Ordinance implementing AB 481 by approving an updated policy for the use of military
  equipment by the Alhambra Police Department. On April 25, 2022, the City Council adopted
  Ordinance No. O2M22-4803 approving a Military Equipment Use Policy (“Policy”) pursuant to
  assembly Bill 481 (“AB 481”). In accordance with the legislation and the Policy, a military
  equipment report must be submitted to the City Council annually for each type of military
  equipment approved within one year of approval, and annually thereafter for as long as the
  military equipment is available for use. Alhambra’s 2024 Annual Military Equipment Report,
  which summarized equipment deployments and purchases during the 2024 calendar year and
  the Police Department’s updated policy, which containd edits to equipment and munition
  inventory numbers and removal of an armored personnel carrier which was initially being
  considered via an Urban Area Security Initiative Grant were outlined in the Chief of Police’s
  staff report dated April 14, 2025. AB 481 requires that the Council determine, based on the
  annual military equipment report submitted pursuant to Section 7072, whether each type of
  military equipment identified in that report has complied with the standards for approval set
  forth in Government Code section 7071(d). Staff reviewed Department records and
  determined there were no complaints or concerns reported on the use of the equipment in
  11

   2024. Additionally, the Department conducted an internal audit and determined that there were
  no violations of the military equipment use policy. The City Council gave first reading to this
  ordinance and approved Alhambra Police Department’s Annual Military Equipment Report set
  forth in the Chief of Police’s April 14, 2025 report per the requirements under Assembly Bill
  481 at the April 14, 2025 Council meeting.

21.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF AN ORDINANCE APPROVING ZONING TEXT
  AMENDMENT AMD-24-02 MAKING GENERAL CLARIFYING UPDATES TO THE CITY’S
ZONING CODE AND ZONING MAP AMENDMENT AMD-25-01 AMENDING THE CITY’S
  ZONING MAP – F2M20-24, O2M25-4844

  Staff requested that the City Council declare introduced for second reading and adopt an
  Ordinance approving Zoning Text Amendment AMD-24-02 making general clarifying
  updates to the City’s Zoning Code and Zoning Map Amendment AMD-25-01 amending the
  City’s Zoning Map. This Zoning Code clean-up included both proposed amendments and
  additions. Proposed amendments consisted of revisions to existing sections of the Alhambra
  Municipal Code (AMC), while the proposed additions would incorporate entirely new sections
  into the AMC. The nature of and reasoning for each proposed amendment and addition could
  be classified by five general categories: 1.) Clarification; 2.) Consistency; 3.) Compliance with
  State laws/Federal laws; 4.) Typographical & Formatting; and 5.) Use Allowances &
  Regulations. Some of the proposed amendments and additions are a combination of these
  five categories. For example, the section on Accessory Dwelling Units was proposed to be
  amended to comply with State law, clarify applicable development standards, and impose new
  regulations pertaining to the Accessory Dwelling Unit uses. Similarly, the addition of a new
  section identifying specific standards for Firearms Sales uses would impose new use
  regulations and would be consistent with Urgency Ordinance No. O2M23-4818, which directed
  staff to provide the City Council with options for additional regulations for such uses. In
  Attachment 1 of the staff report dated April 14, 2025 for this item, each proposed amendment
  and addition is briefly described in a table, which includes a breakdown of the categories
  applicable to each amendment or addition. The City Council gave first reading to this ordinance
  at the April 14, 2025 Council meeting.
